review_comments: It feels like it should be configurable from somewhere, but we might want to at least have it as a constant `DEFAULT_ABORT_CODE` or something like this.

This value doesn't actually matter, because of the SILENT flag -- no error is sent to the peer.

In general though, I do agree we should define DEFAULT_ABORT_CODE or something like that.

Why are we removing close here?
cc @CarnaViire
Because disposing the connection should be sufficient now.

I would not remove it... While disposing *will* close the connection, it would be an abortive closing -- in my view it is mostly a precaution if a user forgot to call graceful CloseAsync. The `RunClientServer` scenario was intended to work gracefully.

If the problem is `ObjectDisposedException` in `Dispose_WithOpenLocalStream_LocalStreamFailsWithQuicOperationAbortedException` maybe it will be better to make closing a no-op if the connection was already disposed?
Yeah, that does seem like a better approach. I'll try to make this work.
